name: Jimi (Nigeria)
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page jimi1255 and reference records 76828 (Shimizu 1978), 657257 (Decker et al. 2022), 136865 (Cosper 1999), 131568 (Jungraithmayr & Ibriszimow 1994)
sources.note: Bibliographic only. No descriptive (grammar/phonology/sketch) reference for jmi; AES moribund. Shimizu 1978 is cited only for subclassification and its language code list does not include jmi.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken; Danladi, Yakubu; Hon, Luther; Aregbesola, Adedamola; Araokanmi, Thelma; Muniru, John; Onoja, David. 2022. A Sociolinguistic Profile of Some Endangered West Chadic B.3 Languages in South Bauchi State, Nigeria with Notes on Dulubu [dbo]. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-019. Dallas: SIL International. 73 pp. (SIL archives 95036)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 8.3 'Phonetic inventories' (pp. 26-27) gives only consonant/vowel charts for the six languages (Jimi lacks [ɣ] and [ɲ]; diphthongs [ua],[ui] only in Jimi). Appendix F (p. 50): 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' 222-item Jimi wordlist (Jimi village, Ganjuwa LGA, 2021) tone-marked impressionistically; Appendix G Jimi noun plurals. a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing. Sec. 3 (pp. 3-4) lists all prior work on Jimi: Gowers 1907, Shimizu 1978, Hansford et al. 1976, Schuh 1978, We…

sources.citation: Newman, Paul. 2022. A Chadic bibliography, 5th ed.
sources.note: Bibliographic only: the only entries keyed [Jimi] are Cosper 1994 South Bauchi Lexicon (Halifax: the author) and Cosper 1999 Barawa Lexicon (LINCOM). No grammar or phonology of Jimi is listed.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Michael Bulkaam. 2021. An introduction to Mantsi, a South Bauchi language of Central Nigeria (draft, KWEF); Caron, Bernard. 2009. Documenting linguistic varieties of the South-Bauchi group; Caron 2005/2009. Les Zaars et leurs voisins
sources.note: Nothing about Jimi: Mantsi paper (sister Boghomic language) mentions Jimi only in its reference list (Cosper n.d., 1999); the two Caron overviews do not mention Jimi at all.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020a. The South Bauchi languages of Central Nigeria: a fresh view based on recent fieldwork. Slides, Colloquium on African Languages and Linguistics 2020.
sources.note: Most recent overview of the group by the one linguist with recent South Bauchi fieldwork; may report unpublished Jimi data or Cosper's unpublished ms; classification/endangerment focus so a stress statement is unlikely.
sources.venue: Slides, Colloquium on African Languages and Linguistics 2020

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019/2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, ed. IV. Entry '220. Jimi'
sources.note: Nothing. Entry: Bauchi State, Darazo LGA; 250 (LA 1971), 400 (1973 SIL); 'Chadic: West sub-branch B: Zaar group'; no references, no phonology. Classification tree lists 'd. Jimi?' under the Boghom subgroup. Same entry (no. 217) in ed. III.

sources.citation: Caron, Bernard. 2002. Review of 'Barawa lexicon: a wordlist of eight South Bauchi (West Chadic) languages: Boghom, Buli, Dott, Geji, Sayanci and Zul' by Ronald Cosper (LINCOM 1999). Chadic Newsletter 23: 46-80. HAL halshs-00644636.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Reports that Cosper 1999 covers 915 items for 8 languages including Jimi, gives phoneme charts for the eight languages in its introduction and marks two tones; the review itself discusses only Zaar and Dott data and judges Cosper's transcriptions unreliable.
Nothing; stub. Alt. name Bi-Gimu; Boghom subgroup; ~1,000 speakers (1995); notes Blench (2006) treats the Zumo (Jum) variety as a separate language.

sources.citation: Cosper, Ronald. 1999. Barawa Lexicon: A wordlist of eight South Bauchi (West Chadic) languages: Boghom, Buli, Dott, Geji, Jimi, Polci, Sayanci and Zul. LINCOM Studies in African Linguistics 39. München: LINCOM. 158 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only published lexicon of Jimi; its introduction has phoneme charts for all eight languages and a note on tone (per Caron 2002); the one place a remark on stress/accent in Jimi could plausibly exist. Data quality judged poor by Caron.

sources.citation: Cosper, Ronald. 1994. South Bauchi Lexicon: a wordlist of nine South Bauchi (West Chadic) languages and dialects. Halifax: the author.
